A revolution, huh...
Hey there. Surprisingly spacious and nice for how it looks outside, isn't it?
Thank you for hooking us up with such a great property.

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: やはり村西さんが社長にはふさわしいんじゃないかと。
examples.trans: Honestly, I think you are the one best suited to be president, Mr. Muranishi.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.trans: You're the right man for the job, Mr. Kawada.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: 分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Godan verb; 持ってくる means 'bring'.
With します, forms お願いします ('please'), the standard polite way to request a service or favor.

examples.text: 一つお願いがあります。
examples.trans: I have one favor to ask.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

examples.text: お願いします。革命だよ、革命。ひっくり返すんだよ。
examples.trans: We're counting on you. It's a revolution—we're going to turn the whole industry upside down!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.
Noun.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
I-adjective describing large area or space.

examples.text: この部屋はとても広いです。
広い庭のある家に住みたいです。
examples.trans: I want to live in a house with a big yard.

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。
村西の件か。求刑三百七十年って事実上の死刑宣告だ。
examples.trans: About Muranishi? Seeking three hundred seventy years is practically a death sentence.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Standalone casual thanks; followed by ございます (present) or ございました (completed occasion) for polite thanks.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。

meanings.note: Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

examples.text: いいんだよ。お前たちの裏本にはさんざん稼がせてもらったからな。
examples.trans: Don't mention it—I made plenty of money off your underground magazines.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: いざとなると、どうしていいか分からなくなって…
examples.trans: Now that the moment is here, I don't know what to do anymore...

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Potential stem + そう (稼げそう) means 'looks like one can earn well'.

examples.text: しっかりお金を稼ぎます。
今月はよく稼げました。
examples.trans: I was able to earn well this month.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').

おく.gloss: do in advance; keep in state

meanings.note: After a te-form (積んでおきました, contracted 入っとけ), indicates doing something in advance or staying put.

examples.text: 窓を開けておきました。
ここに置いておきます。
examples.trans: I will leave it here for now.

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: I-adjective; adverbial form うまく means 'well' or 'smoothly' (as in うまくいく).

examples.text: 計画がうまくいきました。
彼は英語がとてもうまいです。
examples.trans: He is very good at English.

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.note: Calls someone's attention ('look here!') or asks for a brief pause (ちょっと待って).

examples.text: ちょっと待ってください。
ちょっと見てください。

困る.gloss: be troubled; be in a bind

meanings.en: to be troubled; to be in a bind; to have difficulty
meanings.note: Godan verb.

examples.trans: That puts me in a bind.

examples.text: お金がなくて困っている。
examples.trans: I'm in trouble because I have no money.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Attaches to a past-stem verb form to set up a condition ('if a fire starts').

examples.text: 火事になったら大変です。
examples.trans: If a fire breaks out, it will be terrible.

examples.text: 家に帰ったら電話します。
examples.trans: I will call when I get home.

meanings.note: Indefinite pronoun.

examples.text: 分からないことがあれば何でも聞いてください。
examples.trans: If there's anything you don't understand, ask anything.

examples.text: 彼は料理なら何でも作れる。
examples.trans: He can make anything when it comes to cooking.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Everyday reading あした; pairs with また in また明日 ('see you tomorrow').
